subject: Clarifying model-improvement exclusions and subprocessor residency for Novus pilot
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novushealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot DPA question — model improvement & residency evidence

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm two specific things before they move to final approval:

1) Can Redwood commit that data submitted by Novus during the pilot will not be used to improve or retrain Redwood models (no adaptive/model-improvement)? We are looking for contractual language plus an operational proof path we can review.

2) For EU-origin patient data we may route during the pilot, can you describe which subprocessors will touch that data and whether you support an onshore/EU-only processing lane (or SFTP export) for evidence collection?

If you can provide a short evidence pack (ops runbook, subprocessor list, KMS residency statement) that would help speed approvals. We attached our redline of the DPA for context.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and an estimated ETA for the evidence pack.

Best,
Alicia
Director, Data & Privacy
Novus Health

--- Attachment: Novus_DPA_Redline_20260804.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novushealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA question — model improvement & residency evidence

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and for the redline. Quick responses up front:

- Yes — Redwood can commit to an operational "no-model-improvement" configuration for pilot traffic (we call this a non-adaptive serving mode). We can include a contractual amendment point that maps to the DPA section you redlined.

- Evidence pack: we can provide 
  * subprocessor inventory for the pilot,
  * an ops runbook that documents tagging/segregation of pilot traffic,
  * a KMS residency statement and audit log export sample.

Kimberly, can you confirm suggested contract language and whether Legal is comfortable with the DPA redline as a separate addendum?

Karthik, can you prepare the ops evidence pack and a short checklist for EU-only routing options (SFTP vs onshore processing lanes)? If possible, please include which subprocessors would see unredacted EU-origin PII.

Alicia — I expect we can turn a first-pass evidence bundle around in 48-72 hours. Will follow up with the attachments.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA question — model improvement & residency evidence

Hi all,

Attaching an ops-oriented evidence pack for Novus' pilot (see attached ZIP). Highlights below:

- No-improvement configuration:
  * Serving runtime flag: "learning_enabled=false" will be set on the Novus tenant for the pilot.
  * KV/prefix caching retained only for latency; no training pipelines ingesting pilot tokens.
  * Audit: per-request telemetry will be tagged with tenant_id and persistent in an exportable audit log.

- Subprocessor handling and residency:
  * In pilot, compute and inference are routed to our US and EU pools by region. For EU-origin data you can choose:
    - Option A (preferred): EU-onshore inference only (uses our EU GPU pool; subprocessors: EU storage provider (eu-storage.co), EU KMS managed by customer),
    - Option B: Encrypted SFTP export of interaction logs to your SFTP (we will not persist logs in a training store),
  * Subprocessor list for the pilot: eu-storage.co, log-shipper.io, monitoring-corp (US), analytics-lite (US).

- Evidence artifacts included in ZIP:
  * operations_runbook_novus_v1.pdf
  * subprocessor_inventory_pilot.csv
  * kms_residency_statement.txt
  * audit_log_sample_20260805.json (redacted)

Notes/asks:
- We need Novus to confirm which option (A or B) for EU-origin data routing. Option A requires an explicit mention of EU-only routing in the DPA addendum and a mutually agreeable SLA for export requests.
- Kimberly — please advise on the exact DPA clause wording for the non-adaptive commitment. I recommend a short addendum referencing the pilot tenant id and the serving flag.

ETA: evidence ZIP attached. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through any artifacts.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability

--- Attachment: redline_evidence_pack_v1.zip (application/zip, 1.2MB)
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novushealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA question — model improvement & residency evidence

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick replies:

- Novus prefers Option A (EU-onshore inference for EU-origin PII). We'll require the EU KMS residency statement and a confirmation that eu-storage.co will only process EU-origin logs for the pilot.
- We agree the addendum can reference tenant_id NOV-1247 and an ops flag mapping ("learning_enabled=false"). Procurement will accept a short addendum if Legal confirms wording.

Next steps:
- Kimberly, please share suggested language by EOD Monday so procurement can draft the final procurement packet.
- Jonas/Karthik: can you confirm the audit export cadence (daily vs weekly) and retention for the pilot logs? We need daily exports for sampling during the pilot.

If we can close these items and get the evidence pack ingested into our vendor folder, procurement will try to complete approval next week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Alicia
Director, Data & Privacy
Novus Health
